## New Year in Brazil and Peru: Copacabana, Machu Picchu and Titicaca

On this journey, New Year's Eve is celebrated in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), followed by an extensive itinerary across [Peru](/peru/). The program lasts **15 days and 14 nights**, from oceanfront Copacabana through Lima, Cusco and the Inca Sacred Valley to Machu Picchu, high-altitude Titicaca and the desert coast of Paracas.

The main idea is to celebrate the holiday in [Brazil](/brazil/) and then explore several distinct natural zones and historic regions of Peru. This is an eventful journey with flights, road transfers and excursions in the Andes.

## Rio de Janeiro: welcoming the New Year on Copacabana

The first days are devoted to Rio. Sightseeing includes Corcovado and the statue of Christ the Redeemer, as well as Sugarloaf Mountain with its views over the ocean, mountains and beach neighborhoods. In the historic center, travelers discover the Lapa Arches, Selarón Steps and other city landmarks.

The highlight of the Brazilian stage is **New Year's Eve on Copacabana**, one of the world's most famous beaches. Thousands of locals and visitors gather amid the festivities, and fireworks light up the sky at midnight. After the celebrations, the itinerary leaves some time in Rio before the flight to Peru.

Optional activities in the city include a helicopter flight. This is a separate service and must not be assumed to be part of the base tour price.

## Lima, Cusco and the Sacred Valley

After Rio, the route continues to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). You then fly to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and begin exploring the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/). Visits include [Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/), [Maras](/peru/place/maras/) and [Moray](/peru/place/moray/), where historic and agricultural landscapes differ even within the same region.

Altitude becomes an important aspect of the journey. Cusco and the Lake Titicaca region are far above sea level, so active walks should be planned with physical well-being and the pace of ascent in mind. Avoid scheduling the most demanding physical activity immediately after flying into the Andes.

## Machu Picchu and high-altitude Titicaca

The itinerary includes [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), the Inca architectural complex in the Andes and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Steep wooded slopes surround it, with stone structures integrated into the natural terrain. The specific entry circuit and admission time matter when planning a visit.

The route then follows the Route of the Sun through Andean landscapes to [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). Travelers explore the Uros and Taquile islands, local community traditions and the high-altitude lake landscape.

This is a very different experience from New Year's in Rio. Weather and temperatures can change quickly at Titicaca, so warm clothes and the physical demands should be considered in advance.

## Paracas, the Nazca Lines and return to Lima

The final section leads to [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/) on the Pacific coast. The itinerary includes an island nature excursion and the [Nazca Lines](/peru/place/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/) before returning to Lima.

The combination of historical monuments, marine wildlife and desert scenery reveals Peru beyond Cusco and the Andes. Availability of specific marine and flight-based activities depends on excursion conditions and the actual weather.

## Duration and route sequence

| Days | Itinerary |
|---|---|
| 1–5 | Rio and New Year's celebrations |
| 6–7 | Lima, Cusco, Sacred Valley |
| 8–10 | Andes and Machu Picchu |
| 11–12 | Puno, Lake Titicaca |
| 13–15 | Paracas, Nazca, Lima |

The itinerary includes New Year's Eve on December 31 and concludes after the journey through Peru. Booking a specific departure requires aligning the chosen dates with flights and confirmed access to high-altitude sites.

## Price and inclusions

**Tour price: $17,550.** The package includes hotel accommodation with breakfast, scheduled transfers, excursions with a Russian-speaking guide, a rail ticket for Machu Picchu and the entrance tickets specified in the program.

**Flights listed under “Not included” are paid separately, from $1,000 per person.** These include Rio de Janeiro–Lima, Lima–Cusco and Juliaca–Lima flights. Optional excursions should not be regarded as included unless specifically stated.

Hotels may be replaced by others in the same category and the order of excursions may change while retaining the overall contents. When choosing, compare not only prices but also high-altitude sections, the number of transfers and additional expenses.

## Who this New Year's journey suits

The tour suits travelers wishing to combine **a major celebration in Brazil** with Inca history, high-altitude cities and Peru's natural landscapes. It is not designed for people hoping to spend all 15 days on the beach: an intensive sightseeing program follows Rio.

Compare alternatives in the [multi-country travel catalog](/multi-country/) and the [festival and celebration tours](/interests/events-and-festivals/) section.

## Frequently asked questions about the New Year's tour

### How long does the program last?

15 days and 14 nights, starting in Rio and ending in Lima after traveling through Peru.

### Is Machu Picchu included?

Yes. A visit to Machu Picchu is part of the main itinerary, and the inclusions specifically list the rail ticket and entrance tickets according to the program.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. The additional flights listed in the published program cost from $1,000 per person and are paid separately.

## Brazil in 13 days: from Iguazu Falls to white dunes and the ocean

This tour combines regions usually visited on separate journeys. It begins in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and its famous viewpoints, continues to **both sides of Iguazu Falls** and then to the sand dunes of [Lençóis Maranhenses](/brazil/place/lencois-maranhenses/) and the coast near [Praia de Pipa](/brazil/place/praia-de-pipa/).

Over **13 days and 12 nights**, you will see Rio's green mountains, the powerful river at the Argentine border, freshwater lagoons among white sand, the mangrove-lined Preguiças River and beaches in northeastern Brazil. Several domestic flights connect these distant parts of the country.

Although the tour is described as a journey through Brazil, it includes the Argentine side of Iguazu. It therefore involves two countries and requires attention to border-crossing documentation.

## The first days: Rio from Corcovado and Sugarloaf

After arrival in Rio and a hotel transfer, the program includes two full sightseeing days with a Russian-speaking guide. One takes you to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado through [Tijuca Forest](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/). The other features the cable car from [Praia Vermelha](/brazil/place/praia-vermelha/) to Sugarloaf Mountain, as well as a tour of the historic center.

These included excursions reveal different sides of Rio, but there is no long free beach section here. Most time relaxing by the ocean is scheduled for the end of the journey.

On day four, a transfer to the airport and flight to Foz do Iguaçu are planned. This distinguishes the route from tours focusing entirely on the northeastern coast: you first visit one of South America's major natural landmarks before continuing to the dunes.

## Two days at Iguazu: why both sides matter

Day five includes the [Brazilian side of Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) with a Russian-speaking guide. Observation trails provide views of cascades amid rainforest and the Devil's Throat gorge. On day six, the tour visits Argentina, near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), where viewing platforms, an ecological train and walkways offer different perspectives of individual waterfalls.

These are **two separate sightseeing days**, not a repeat of the same visit. The Brazilian side gives sweeping panoramic views; the Argentine side lets visitors get closer to the cascades. Planning requires allowing time for the border crossing and applying the entry requirements relevant to the traveler's citizenship.

On day seven, the journey continues with a flight to [São Luís](/brazil/place/sao-luis/), where the northeastern section begins.

## Lençóis Maranhenses: seasonal lagoons and white dunes

Day eight includes a drive from São Luís to [Barreirinhas](/brazil/place/barreirinhas/), taking approximately **3.5 hours**, followed by a group excursion with an English-speaking guide to [Lençóis Maranhenses](/brazil/place/lencois-maranhenses/). The national park is famous for its white dunes, with freshwater lagoons filling between them after rainfall.

**The season changes the very nature of this experience.** Lagoons tend to be fuller after the rains; in drier periods, individual pools may become shallow or disappear. When choosing dates, consider not only beach and sightseeing weather but also whether you want to see water among the dunes. Exact conditions depend on actual rainfall that season.

Days nine and ten continue the exploration. A boat excursion on the Preguiças River includes stops at Vassouras, the lighthouse area and [Atins](/brazil/place/atins/). The program then visits Atins Lagoon before returning to Barreirinhas. These trips show that Lençóis is more than sand ridges: the region also has a river, mangroves, villages and coastal scenery.

## Pipa: the final two days beside the ocean

Day eleven includes returning toward São Luís airport, flying to [Natal](/brazil/place/natal/) and transferring to [Praia de Pipa](/brazil/place/praia-de-pipa/). Day twelve is free for relaxation in the resort village, surrounded by sandy beaches, ocean cliffs and green stretches of coast.

It is an enjoyable ending to an eventful trip, but **the 13-day itinerary is not a long beach vacation**: Pipa has just one fully free day without a fixed sightseeing program. Day thirteen is devoted to the transfer to Natal airport.

If your priority is the ocean, other [Ada Tours beach itineraries](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/) allow comparisons of free-day proportions, while [nature and wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/) include other natural landmarks.

## Flights, guides and services included

The Rio and Iguazu sections provide **private excursions with a Russian-speaking guide**. Around Barreirinhas, excursions are **group activities with an English-speaking guide**. Transfers are listed as private except for the São Luís–Barreirinhas–São Luís portion, which uses a group arrangement. These distinctions matter to those who require private guiding throughout the itinerary.

Hotels, specified transfers and scheduled excursions are included. **International flights and domestic flights along the Rio–Iguazu–São Luís–Natal route are not included in the base package.** Optional excursions and meals or drinks during transfers are listed separately. The tour price starts at **USD 5,345**, but comparisons should take into account which flights travelers must pay for themselves.

| Stage | Program feature |
|---|---|
| Rio | Private excursions to two viewpoints |
| Iguazu | Two excursion days in Brazil and Argentina |
| Lençóis | Group trips to dunes and lagoons |
| Preguiças and Atins | River excursions and small villages |
| Pipa | Ocean relaxation before departure |

## Frequently asked questions about Brazil's dunes and beaches

### When is the best time to see the lagoons of Lençóis Maranhenses?

The fullest lagoons are generally found after seasonal rainfall. Water levels vary each year, so dates should be chosen with actual seasonal conditions in mind rather than a fixed promotional calendar.

### Is the Argentine side of Iguazu included?

Yes. It is scheduled as a separate excursion on day six. Document requirements depend on the traveler's citizenship.

### How much time is allocated to Pipa's beaches?

After arriving from Natal, the itinerary includes one full free day at the resort, followed by an airport transfer. For a longer beach stay, consider a program with fewer regional flights.

### Are all excursions led by a Russian-speaking guide?

No. Private excursions in Rio and Iguazu have Russian-speaking guides, while around Barreirinhas the group activities have English-speaking guidance.

## Brazil and Argentina in 14 days: gold-rush towns, beaches and Iguazu

The “Brazil in 14 Days” route differs from a conventional journey through Rio and the waterfalls. It includes the historic towns of [Ouro Preto](/brazil/place/ouro-preto/) and [Mariana](/brazil/place/mariana/), the museum and botanical grounds of [Inhotim](/brazil/place/inhotim/), the Afro-Brazilian heritage of [Salvador](/brazil/place/salvador/) and **three days of relaxed beach time** at [Praia do Forte](/brazil/place/praia-do-forte/).

The tour lasts **14 days and 13 nights**. The first days focus on Rio, followed by the historic Minas Gerais route, a flight to Bahia, relaxation by the ocean and the final stage at Iguazu Falls. The last section includes **the Argentine side of the falls**, not only Brazil. This makes the journey a multi-country itinerary even though the principal name lists Brazilian destinations.

## Rio de Janeiro: Sugarloaf and Corcovado

The journey begins in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The first three days cover arrival and two excursions. On one day, travelers ascend Sugarloaf Mountain via Morro da Urca. On the other, they travel to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado through [Tijuca Forest](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/).

Visiting Rio's two iconic viewpoints on separate days is convenient for travelers wanting photographs from different sides of the city, an understanding of its natural setting and time for history rather than one hurried sightseeing round. Day four includes an extended drive toward Minas Gerais, stopping at [Petrópolis](/brazil/place/petropolis/), formerly the summer residence city of the imperial family.

## Minas Gerais: gold mines, Baroque architecture and modern art

The historic stage centers on [Ouro Preto](/brazil/place/ouro-preto/), a town of steep cobblestone streets and churches preserving the memory of gold mining. Its historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The itinerary also includes [Congonhas](/brazil/place/congonhas/), [Mariana](/brazil/place/mariana/) and the former Passagem de Mina gold mine.

This is a cultural tour, not a specialist mining expedition with fieldwork. The excursions reveal how precious-metal extraction influenced colonial architecture, urban life and art.

Another major stop is [Inhotim](/brazil/place/inhotim/), a contemporary art museum set in a botanical landscape. It extends the story in a surprising direction: after Ouro Preto's Baroque churches, you walk among contemporary artworks, greenery and pavilions. The route then proceeds to Belo Horizonte for the flight to Salvador.

## Salvador and Praia do Forte: Bahia's history and unhurried days

In [Salvador](/brazil/place/salvador/), the itinerary includes an excursion through historic neighborhoods. Visits cover Pelourinho, churches, the Lacerda Elevator and Mercado Modelo. Afro-Brazilian cultural traditions are particularly evident, and the city's architecture differs from the historic settlements of Minas Gerais.

**An important guiding condition:** the Salvador excursion is specified with an **English-speaking guide**. Russian-language guiding can be discussed separately. General references to Russian-speaking excursions elsewhere do not change this requirement.

After Salvador, the group transfers to [Praia do Forte](/brazil/place/praia-do-forte/). Days eight to ten are reserved for beaches, walks and relaxation. The area is associated with sea turtle conservation, and other marine animals can be seen offshore in suitable seasons. However, turtle or whale watching must not be treated as a guaranteed paid excursion unless specifically included in the program.

If an extended beach holiday is your main goal, compare this trip with other [beach tours](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/). Here the beach is one part of the itinerary, not all 14 days.

## Iguazu: both sides of the falls at the end of the journey

On day eleven, after a transfer back to Salvador, travelers fly to Foz do Iguaçu. Day twelve is devoted to the Brazilian side of [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), offering sweeping panoramas of cascades and the gorge. On day thirteen, the tour crosses into Argentina, near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/).

The difference between the two sides becomes clear on the excursions: the Brazilian side offers the whole panorama, while walkways on the Argentine side lead closer to the individual cascades. An airport transfer is scheduled for day fourteen.

For this cross-border visit, travelers must consider their own documents and current entry rules in advance. The program does not impose one universal requirement on all nationalities; conditions are checked individually before departure.

## What's included and how to assess the price

The package includes hotels with breakfast, chauffeured transfers, excursions with the stated guides and entrance tickets. The starting price is **USD 7,357**. The calculation needs to be assessed alongside the chosen accommodation format and services.

**Domestic flights are paid for separately**, including the Belo Horizonte–Salvador–Foz do Iguaçu segments, as well as optional excursions, additional food and drinks. International airfare and other costs must be clarified in an individual offer; do not assume international tickets are included merely because they are absent from a short exclusions list.

| Itinerary section | What travelers experience |
|---|---|
| Rio | Famous viewpoints and urban leisure |
| Minas Gerais | Gold-mining history and Baroque art |
| Salvador | Afro-Brazilian culture |
| Praia do Forte | Several beach days |
| Iguazu | Brazilian and Argentine waterfalls |

This tour is particularly suited to travelers wanting history, architecture and beaches in one journey. Those who prefer natural trails and fewer museums may want to consider other [Brazil itineraries](/brazil/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about historic Brazil

### Why does this route include Argentina?

An excursion to the Argentine side of Iguazu is scheduled for day thirteen. Travelers cross the border to see the falls, although most cities and overnight stays are in Brazil.

### Is the program suitable for museum lovers?

Yes. Its principal cultural section covers Minas Gerais history, religious architecture, a former mine, the Inhotim museum and Salvador. Several days are nevertheless free for beach relaxation.

### Is there a Russian-speaking guide in Salvador?

The source program specifies an English-speaking guide in Salvador. Russian-language guiding would require separate agreement.

### Should I budget for domestic flights?

Yes. Flights on the specified Belo Horizonte–Salvador–Foz do Iguaçu segments are explicitly excluded from the base price.

## Brazil in 12 days: cities, Iguazu and the Atlantic coast

This journey alternates city and nature experiences with little repetition. The first days are spent in [São Paulo](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/), followed by Iguazu Falls on both sides of the international border, [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and the concluding section on [Ilha Grande](/brazil/place/ilha-grande/) and in [Paraty](/brazil/place/paraty/).

The program lasts **12 days and 11 nights**. Its greatest appeal is the succession of distinct experiences: a vast metropolis, rainforest waterfalls, urban panoramas, boat excursions, historic streets and quiet beaches. This requires several hotel changes and domestic flights.

Although the name emphasizes Brazil, **one excursion day takes place in Argentina**. Travelers must therefore account for the border crossing and the documentation requirements applicable to their citizenship.

## São Paulo and Iguazu: the first four days

In São Paulo, a Russian-speaking guide leads an excursion through the historic center and modern neighborhoods. It includes the cathedral, Japanese district, Municipal Market, Paulista Avenue and Ibirapuera Park. This is a useful introduction to Brazil before the more nature-focused part of the trip.

On day three, the group flies to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and visits the Brazilian side of the waterfalls. Local trails provide broad views of the cascades and forested gorge. On day four, travelers cross the border to the Argentine side near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), where trails and walkways bring them closer to individual falls, including the Devil's Throat area.

The two visits complement each other. Brazil offers panoramic views; Argentina provides multiple observation points and longer walks above the water. Iguazu is not treated as one quick stop lasting a few hours: the program allocates **two excursion days**.

## Rio de Janeiro: two classic panoramas

After flying to Rio, the itinerary includes two separate sightseeing days with a Russian-speaking guide. The first focuses on Sugarloaf Mountain: the cable car begins near [Praia Vermelha](/brazil/place/praia-vermelha/), passes through Urca and reaches a viewpoint over Guanabara Bay. A tour of Rio's historic center is also scheduled.

The following day leads to Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer. The train ascends through the green landscape of [Tijuca](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/), while the upper viewpoint overlooks the ocean, bay and mountains. The program places Sugarloaf and Corcovado on separate days so that exploring the city does not become a hurried transfer between viewpoints.

For travelers wanting more time in the city, see other [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/). Rio is a substantial stage on this itinerary, after which the journey continues toward a quieter stretch of coastline.

## Ilha Grande and Paraty: why boats matter

On day eight, the journey from Rio to [Ilha Grande](/brazil/place/ilha-grande/) combines road transport with **a shared boat**. The island has no ordinary car traffic, so the pace changes on arrival. Day nine is devoted to a schooner excursion with beach stops and opportunities to swim. The original program specifies that this trip is **without an accompanying guide**, which is useful to know in advance.

On day ten, a shared boat and road transfer take travelers to [Paraty](/brazil/place/paraty/). The historic center retains colonial streets and architecture connected with the old gold trade route. Paraty and part of Ilha Grande's natural areas belong to the UNESCO World Heritage property “Paraty and Ilha Grande – Culture and Biodiversity.” This is one reason the pairing of island and historic port offers more than a conventional beach stop.

Day eleven features a group excursion to [Trindade](/brazil/place/trindade-paraty/) and several beaches, including Praia do Cepilho, Praia dos Ranchos and Praia do Meio. The last day consists of an airport transfer to São Paulo for the return flight.

## Private and group services: what is actually included

We offer a private tour, but **not every service is exclusively private**. Excursions with Russian-speaking guides in São Paulo, Iguazu and Rio are provided privately. Group services and boat transport are used on Ilha Grande and in Paraty, and on the island this is a natural part of the logistics.

| Stage | Main arrangement |
|---|---|
| São Paulo, Iguazu, Rio | Private guided excursions |
| Ilha Grande | Shared boat transfers and excursion |
| Paraty, Trindade | Group services and excursion |

The price includes hotel stays with breakfast and the specified transfers. **International and domestic flights are paid for separately**, as are insurance, tips and personal expenses. The tour starts at **USD 3,580**; the detailed pricing terms must be checked for the specific travelers.

## Frequently asked questions about the 12-day itinerary

### Why is this considered a multi-country journey?

The program visits the Argentine side of Iguazu Falls. Most overnight stays and visits are in Brazil, but the border-crossing day requires following Argentina's entry rules.

### How many days are needed for Iguazu Falls?

This tour includes two days, first on the Brazilian side and then on the Argentine side, allowing travelers to experience both wide panoramas and close views of the cascades.

### Is a car needed on Ilha Grande?

Visitors mainly travel on foot and by boat. The program already provides the boat crossing, so a private car on the island is unnecessary.

### Are all excursions conducted by a Russian-speaking guide?

No. Russian-speaking guidance is included on private excursions in São Paulo, Iguazu and Rio. The Ilha Grande boat trip is specified without a guide, and services in Paraty are organized as group activities.

## Buenos Aires, Salta and Iguazu in 12 days: who this itinerary suits

The [12-day Ada Tours journey](/multi-country/tour/buenos-aires-salta-iguazu/) combines [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), northwestern Argentina and Iguazu Falls on both sides of the border. Travelers begin by exploring the neighborhoods and history of Argentina's capital, then continue to the [Salta](/argentina/place/salta/) region with vineyards, colorful mountains and salt flats. The final days focus on [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/).

**The main countries on this route are Argentina and Brazil.** Uruguay appears among possible optional excursions from Buenos Aires, but the 12-day itinerary contains no mandatory Uruguayan stage. Keep this distinction in mind when comparing it with tours that actually include multiple nights in Uruguay.

## The itinerary by region

| Days | Main stage |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Buenos Aires |
| 4–7 | Salta and surroundings |
| 8–10 | Iguazu Falls |
| 11–12 | Buenos Aires and departure |

The first days include a private transfer, a Buenos Aires sightseeing tour and time for optional activities. Sites on the program include 9 de Julio Avenue, the Obelisk, Plaza de Mayo, Casa Rosada, San Telmo, La Boca and Recoleta. Optional excursions may take you to Tigre, a gaucho ranch or [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) for a day, crossing from Argentina. These additions are arranged separately.

The journey then moves to northwestern Argentina. [Cafayate](/argentina/place/cafayate/) is associated with winemaking, [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/) and [Quebrada de Humahuaca](/argentina/place/quebrada-de-humahuaca/) with colorful rock formations, and [Salinas Grandes](/argentina/place/salinas-grandes/) with high-altitude salt flats. This sequence involves long drives and considerable changes in altitude, so it is best evaluated in terms of actual travel time and the accessibility of stops.

## The Argentine and Brazilian sides of Iguazu

The itinerary allocates separate days to the national parks around the falls. On the Argentine side, visitors explore a system of trails and viewpoints; the Brazilian side provides another perspective on many of the cascades. [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) are distinct cities and geographic places, even though they serve the same natural region.

Access to particular walking trails can change due to river levels, boardwalk maintenance and park management decisions. In September 2026, the Argentine national park authority reported the precautionary removal of walkways on the trail to Devil's Throat while other paths remained open. The precise list of viewpoints should therefore be checked before the travel date rather than treating every named trail as guaranteed.

## Included services and separate expenses

The tour lasts **12 days and 11 nights** and includes accommodation in 4-star hotels with breakfast and local taxes, private excursions, chauffeured private transfers and national park admission. Private Russian-speaking guides are provided in Buenos Aires and Iguazu, while private English-speaking guides accompany the Salta stage. International and domestic flights, optional excursions, gratuities, early check-in and late check-out are paid for separately.

Compare the core itinerary with the [Argentina tour catalog](/argentina/tour/) and [multi-country journeys](/multi-country/): northwestern Argentina, Cafayate and the salt flats take time, so this option differs from programs covering only Buenos Aires and Iguazu.

## Frequently asked questions about the route

### Is Uruguay a mandatory part of the trip?

No. [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) in Uruguay is listed among possible optional excursions. The main itinerary is through Argentina and Brazil.

### Can I see both sides of Iguazu Falls?

Yes. Separate days are scheduled for the Argentine and Brazilian sides. Access to particular trails depends on current park management decisions.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. Domestic flights, like international tickets, are paid for separately. The overland program and guiding are included to the agreed extent.
